deck.title: The Characteristic Properties of Acids & Bases

front_blocks.md: Define "acid" in terms of the ions it produces in aqueous solution.

back_blocks.md: An acid is a substance that produces **hydrogen ions**, H<sup>+</sup> (aq), when dissolved in water.

cards.front_md: Define "acid" in terms of the ions it produces in aqueous solution.
cards.back_md: An acid is a substance that produces **hydrogen ions**, H<sup>+</sup> (aq), when dissolved in water.

front_blocks.md: On the pH scale, acids have a pH **..........** 7 and alkalis have a pH **..........** 7.

back_blocks.md: On the pH scale, acids have a pH **below** 7 and alkalis have a pH **above** 7.

cards.front_md: On the pH scale, acids have a pH **..........** 7 and alkalis have a pH **..........** 7.
cards.back_md: On the pH scale, acids have a pH **below** 7 and alkalis have a pH **above** 7.

front_blocks.md: What three products form when an acid reacts with a metal carbonate?

back_blocks.md: When an acid reacts with a metal carbonate / salt, **carbon dioxide** and **water** are produced.

cards.front_md: What three products form when an acid reacts with a metal carbonate?
cards.back_md: When an acid reacts with a metal carbonate / salt, **carbon dioxide** and **water** are produced.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
All bases are alkalis.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
A base is any substance that neutralises an acid, but only bases that dissolve in water are called alkalis.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

All bases are alkalis.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

A base is any substance that neutralises an acid, but only bases that dissolve in water are called alkalis.

front_blocks.md: What is an alkali?

back_blocks.md: An alkali is a **soluble base** that produces **hydroxide ions**, OH<sup>-</sup> (aq), when dissolved in water.

cards.front_md: What is an alkali?
cards.back_md: An alkali is a **soluble base** that produces **hydroxide ions**, OH<sup>-</sup> (aq), when dissolved in water.

front_blocks.md: When sodium hydroxide dissolves in water it dissociates to form Na<sup>+</sup> (aq) and **..........** (aq) ions, making the solution **..........** .

back_blocks.md: When sodium hydroxide dissolves in water it dissociates to form Na<sup>+</sup> (aq) and **OH**<sup>**^-^**</sup> (aq) ions, making the solution **alkaline**.

cards.front_md: When sodium hydroxide dissolves in water it dissociates to form Na<sup>+</sup> (aq) and **..........** (aq) ions, making the solution **..........** .
cards.back_md: When sodium hydroxide dissolves in water it dissociates to form Na<sup>+</sup> (aq) and **OH**<sup>**^-^**</sup> (aq) ions, making the solution **alkaline**.

front_blocks.md: How does litmus indicator change colour in acidic and alkaline solutions?

back_blocks.md: In acidic solutions litmus turns **red**. In alkaline solutions litmus turns **blue**.

cards.front_md: How does litmus indicator change colour in acidic and alkaline solutions?
cards.back_md: In acidic solutions litmus turns **red**. In alkaline solutions litmus turns **blue**.

front_blocks.md: State the net ionic equation for all acid-base neutralisation reactions.

back_blocks.md: The net ionic equation is:

cards.front_md: State the net ionic equation for all acid-base neutralisation reactions.
cards.back_md:
The net ionic equation is:

**H**<sup>**+**</sup>** (aq) + OH**<sup>**-**</sup>** (aq) → H**<sub>**2**</sub>**O (l)**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
All reactions of acids are neutralisation reactions.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
When a metal reacts with an acid, a salt is produced but no water is formed, so it does not count as a neutralisation reaction.

cards.front_md:

cards.back_md:
**False.**

front_blocks.md: The pH scale runs from 1 to 14. A pH of **..........** is neutral, a pH below 7 is **..........** and a pH above 7 is **..........** .

back_blocks.md: The pH scale runs from 1 to 14. A pH of **7** is neutral, a pH below 7 is **acidic** and a pH above 7 is **alkaline**.

cards.front_md: The pH scale runs from 1 to 14. A pH of **..........** is neutral, a pH below 7 is **..........** and a pH above 7 is **..........** .
cards.back_md: The pH scale runs from 1 to 14. A pH of **7** is neutral, a pH below 7 is **acidic** and a pH above 7 is **alkaline**.

front_blocks.md: Why does a solution become neutral when an acid and an alkali react in a neutralisation reaction?

back_blocks.md: The solution becomes neutral because **H**<sup>**+**</sup>** ions** from the acid react with **OH**<sup>**-**</sup>** ions** from the alkali to form **water**, removing both types of ion from solution.

cards.front_md: Why does a solution become neutral when an acid and an alkali react in a neutralisation reaction?
cards.back_md: The solution becomes neutral because **H**<sup>**+**</sup>** ions** from the acid react with **OH**<sup>**-**</sup>** ions** from the alkali to form **water**, removing both types of ion from solution.

front_blocks.md: What does it mean for the pH scale to be logarithmic?

back_blocks.md: Each change of 1 on the pH scale represents a change in hydrogen ion concentration by a **factor of 10**.

cards.front_md: What does it mean for the pH scale to be logarithmic?
cards.back_md: Each change of 1 on the pH scale represents a change in hydrogen ion concentration by a **factor of 10**.

back_blocks.md: Universal indicator is a mixture of **indicators** used to estimate **pH** by matching colour to a chart.

front_blocks.md: How does the concentration of H<sup>+</sup> ions relate to pH?

back_blocks.md: As the concentration of H<sup>+</sup> ions increases, the pH **decreases** — they have an **inverse** relationship.

front_blocks.md: Define "acidic oxide" and give two examples.

back_blocks.md: An acidic oxide is formed when a **non-metal** combines with oxygen. Examples include **CO**<sub>**2**</sub> and **SO**<sub>**2**</sub>.

cards.front_md: Define "acidic oxide" and give two examples.
cards.back_md: An acidic oxide is formed when a **non-metal** combines with oxygen. Examples include **CO**<sub>**2**</sub> and **SO**<sub>**2**</sub>.

front_blocks.md: Metal oxides are **..........** oxides; non-metal oxides are **..........** oxides.

back_blocks.md: Metal oxides are **basic** oxides; non-metal oxides are **acidic** oxides.

cards.front_md: Metal oxides are **..........** oxides; non-metal oxides are **..........** oxides.
cards.back_md: Metal oxides are **basic** oxides; non-metal oxides are **acidic** oxides.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Basic oxides dissolve in water to produce a low pH solution.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Basic oxides dissolve in water to produce an alkaline (basic) solution with a high pH, not a low one.

front_blocks.md: What is an amphoteric oxide?

back_blocks.md: An amphoteric oxide can react as **both an acid and a base**, depending on its reactant. In both cases a salt and water are formed.

cards.front_md: What is an amphoteric oxide?
cards.back_md: An amphoteric oxide can react as **both an acid and a base**, depending on its reactant. In both cases a salt and water are formed.

front_blocks.md: Why is zinc oxide (ZnO) described as amphoteric?

back_blocks.md: Zinc oxide is amphoteric because it reacts with **both acids and bases**, forming a salt and water in each case.

cards.front_md: Why is zinc oxide (ZnO) described as amphoteric?
cards.back_md: Zinc oxide is amphoteric because it reacts with **both acids and bases**, forming a salt and water in each case.

front_blocks.md: Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> reacts with HCl to form **..........** and water, behaving as a **..........** oxide.

back_blocks.md: Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> reacts with HCl to form **AlCl**<sub>**3**</sub> and water, behaving as a **basic** oxide.

cards.front_md: Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> reacts with HCl to form **..........** and water, behaving as a **..........** oxide.
cards.back_md: Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> reacts with HCl to form **AlCl**<sub>**3**</sub> and water, behaving as a **basic** oxide.

front_blocks.md: What are neutral oxides and give two examples?

back_blocks.md: Neutral oxides do not react with acids or bases. Examples include **N**<sub>**2**</sub>**O** and **CO**.
